chunks: And if a disaster were to befall them for what their hands have sent before, they would say: 'Our Lord, why did You not send us a Messenger so we could follow Your signs and be among the believers?'

key_terms.بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ: for what their hands have sent before (consequences of their deeds)

ai.seo_question: Why do people often only seek faith when disaster strikes?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse illustrates the psychological state of 'heedlessness' (ghaflah) where divine signs are ignored until a tangible calamity serves as a wake-up call. It underscores the human tendency to delay repentance until suffering becomes immediate, highlighting the mercy of sending Prophets to prevent such last-minute regret. This reflects the broader theological principle that guidance is a divine gift, yet its acceptance is often contingent upon experiential consequence.
